summary: Full ContextBench run (1,132 scored rows, 66 repositories) through tools/retrieval-bench. corvint query has the highest file and line precision of the ranking arms but the lowest file and line recall (coverage); corvint context has the highest recall. Both use 1-3 percent of the bytes of the baselines' top-20 files. Reported unrepaired.

refused_rows.reason: empty problem_statement; the adapter refuses a row with no query text

repositories.method: git clone --bare into its own new empty directory on the Windows-box WSL2 host; refs_sha256 is sha256 of `git for-each-ref --format='%(objectname) %(refname)'`

corvint.note: linux/amd64 source build of the lane base, not a release asset

run.host: Windows box WSL2 Ubuntu, offline local inputs (CEP-V0-003)
run.sharding: rows split into 16-row shards, later 4-row shards and, for pending mui/material-ui shards that timed out at 480 s under host load, 1-row shards. Superseded shard files were moved aside unscored; the sorted scored row-set digest is unchanged. Each row was scored exactly once.

metric_definitions.cb_file_coverage: ContextBench file recall: gold files present in the arm's answer / gold files (CEP-V0-002)
metric_definitions.cb_file_precision: answer files that are gold / answer files
metric_definitions.cb_line_coverage: gold line spans covered by the answer's line spans / gold line spans
metric_definitions.cb_line_precision: answer lines inside gold spans / answer lines; a lower bound, because a ranking-only arm answers whole files
metric_definitions.recall@k, precision@k, mrr@k, hit@k: file-level ranking metrics over the top-20 list
metric_definitions.abstained: fraction of rows where the arm returned no answer
metric_definitions.means: unweighted means over rows; cb_* means cover error-free arm answers only (CEP-V0-002), itt_errors_as_zero scores errored rows as 0
metric_definitions.bytes: corvint and context: packet_bytes the adapter recorded; baselines: sum of `git cat-file -s` over the top-20 ranked paths at base_commit (paths absent at base_commit count 0, so baseline bytes are a lower bound)

bm25:all.bytes_source: sum of git cat-file -s over top-20 ranked files at base_commit (0 when abstained)

bm25:ident.bytes_source: sum of git cat-file -s over top-20 ranked files at base_commit (0 when abstained)

grep.bytes_source: sum of git cat-file -s over top-20 ranked files at base_commit (0 when abstained)

grep-ident.bytes_source: sum of git cat-file -s over top-20 ranked files at base_commit (0 when abstained)

observations: corvint query: file recall 0.245 and line recall 0.282, below every baseline (grep 0.318/0.366, bm25:all 0.375/0.422, grep-ident 0.357/0.387); file precision 0.255 is above grep and bm25:all but below grep-ident (0.391) and bm25:ident (0.299).
corvint query returns at most 12 files (median 4; 142 empty answers = 114 abstentions + 28 errors), so recall@10 equals recall@20 (0.239) and the top-20 budget is mostly unused.
corvint context: file recall 0.483 and line recall 0.537, the highest of all arms, with 15.8 KB mean packets against 387 KB to 1.45 MB of top-20 baseline files.

Paired on file recall, corvint query loses to every baseline (for example 169 wins, 465 losses, 498 ties against bm25:all); corvint context wins against every baseline (for example 410 wins, 145 losses, 577 ties against bm25:all).

not_run.reason: ContextBench rows carry no changed_file, so the change-anchored arms have no input
the adapter records latency NOT_RUN (COLD_UNIQUE / NOT_APPLICABLE); the box ran at load average 50-120 from other work, so wall_ms medians are descriptive only

limits: CEP-V0-006 forbids committing report files and bench data; this receipt is an aggregate. Per-shard reports and row data stay on the measurement host.
CEP-V0-006: evidence, not promotion; no ranking default or product claim changes.
Line precision is a lower bound for every arm.
Baseline bytes are a lower bound: paths absent at base_commit are counted as 0 bytes.
